title: Veterans Pension Care-Cost Adjustments — Insurance Premiums by Date of Last Confirmation
content:
# Training note: insurance premiums in a Veterans Pension care-cost rate adjustment

In a care-cost rate adjustment, insurance premiums on the Veterans Pension award count by how recently they were last confirmed. They were last confirmed by the most recent rate adjustment on the award (the date it was recorded) or, when the award has none, by the grant of the award (the date the award was opened). The age is counted in days to the date of the adjustment.

| Last confirmed | Premiums counted |
|---|---|
| within one year: 365 days or fewer | the medical expense figure on the award, in full |
| more than 365 days but no more than two years (730 days) | only the standard Medicare Part B premium of 202.90 a month, for 12 months, for each member of the household the rate category covers |
| more than 730 days | nothing — premiums add nothing until the veteran reports them again |

Household members covered: 2 in a rate category that counts spouse income (the one-dependent categories), 1 in a category that does not (the no-dependent categories).

## Questions and answers

**What does the middle band come to?** 202.90 multiplied by 12 is 2434.80 for a household of 1; multiplied by 2 members it is 4869.60.

**Which date counts when the award has had rate adjustments?** The most recent rate adjustment's recording date; the grant date is used only when the award carries no rate adjustment.

**Hypothetical case.** An award granted 500 days ago with no rate adjustment and a medical expense figure of 3100.00, in Veterans Pension (Housebound, One Dependent): 500 days falls in the middle band, so 4869.60 is counted, not 3100.00. Had the award been granted 365 days ago, 3100.00 would be counted; at 731 days, nothing.
